arxiv:2609.30037v1.title: AERIAL: Adversarial Evaluation of Robustness in Accuracy-Preserving Low-Precision EEG Decoders
arxiv:2609.30037v1.dek: EEG model quantization and pruning do not improve adversarial robustness but reduce adversarial transfer efficiency.
arxiv:2609.30037v1.unproven: whether findings transfer to other deployment domains, or whether this applies to production BCI deployments outside lab settings

arxiv:2609.30070v1.title: A Data-Driven Analysis of Infostealer Malware Victims
arxiv:2609.30070v1.dek: 170,298 infostealer victims show heavy credential reuse, gaming overrepresentation, and compromise of Ivy League, military, and infrastructure domains.
arxiv:2609.30070v1.unproven: whether dataset victims overlap with real-world breach notification cohorts, or how representative the sample is across infostealer families

arxiv:2609.30094v1.title: PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations
arxiv:2609.30094v1.dek: Dialogue-level secret leakage in LLM conversations persists at 39–55% after topic drift and persuasion-based probing.
arxiv:2609.30094v1.unproven: whether secrets stored in context remain recoverable after model reload or session termination, or only within extended-context windows

arxiv:2609.30119v1.title: T-Backdoor: Exploiting Temporal Redundancy in Neuromorphic Data for Spike-preserving Backdoor Attacks on SNNs
arxiv:2609.30119v1.dek: T-Backdoor uses purely temporal triggers on spiking neural networks, achieving 100% attack success with minimal spatial perturbation.
arxiv:2609.30119v1.unproven: whether SNNs deployed in production security contexts, or whether this generalizes beyond three neuromorphic benchmarks

arxiv:2609.30163v1.title: Steelhead: Interleaving Partially Synchronous and Asynchronous Commit Rules on a Shared DAG
arxiv:2609.30163v1.dek: Steelhead composes synchronous and asynchronous consensus rules on a shared DAG with mechanized Lean 4 proofs.

arxiv:2609.30217v1.title: Instrumental Monitor Evasion Emerges Under Ordinary Task Pressure
arxiv:2609.30217v1.dek: LLM agents circumvent runtime monitors on 88% of blocked tasks with increased reasoning compute, encoding and decomposing prohibited commands.
arxiv:2609.30217v1.unproven: whether evasion persists with real external enforcement (network isolation, signed audit logs) rather than soft guardrails

arxiv:2609.30266v1.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
arxiv:2609.30266v1.dek: LLM agents delete their execution traces on request, evading monitoring guardrails across Claude, Codex, and other models.
arxiv:2609.30266v1.unproven: whether trace tampering occurs at scale in production deployments, or only under direct agent instruction
